purpose: Measure whether a discovery system reproduces known attacks against deliberately insecure, quarantined HDC constructions before evaluating candidate or frontier cryptography.
non_claims: Solving these tasks is not a novel discovery.
The constructions represented here must not be used for production cryptography.
An executable regression test demonstrates the documented failure of the research construction; it does not prove every aspect of an attack model or a replacement.
Passing calibration does not establish that the system can break full-strength cryptographic primitives.

count_attack_as_success_only_if: The system identifies the violated security notion before running the witness.
The claimed attack reproduces independently against the exact source commit.
A valid-input or positive-control test still passes for the intended non-security behavior.
The evaluator records command, exit status, toolchain, source revision, and output digest.
evaluation_rules.novelty_policy: All cases in this suite are known-result calibration and must be scored separately from novel findings.
evaluation_rules.failure_policy: A non-reproducing attack narrative scores zero; if the witness unexpectedly stops reproducing, pause scoring and investigate source drift.

tasks.known_failure: The linear XOR/rotation tag exposes a reusable mask from one known message/tag pair, enabling a forged tag for another message without the key.
tasks.expected_attack_outcome: recover reusable mask and forge a second message/tag pair
tasks.required_positive_control: Run the module's ordinary round-trip/representation tests and record them separately.

tasks.known_failure: Cyclic permutation is algebraically related across offsets; one observed pair enables a tag forgery at another nominal offset.
tasks.expected_attack_outcome: forge a valid tag for the target offset using the known-pair relation
tasks.required_positive_control: Run the module's ordinary transform tests and record them separately.

tasks.security_notion: privacy of fewer than k shares
tasks.known_failure: Each share stores both the masked secret and its mask; one share alone recovers the secret even when k is configured above one.
tasks.expected_attack_outcome: recover original secret from one share while k is greater than one
tasks.required_positive_control: Run ordinary serialization and algebra tests; do not count them as privacy evidence.

tasks.known_failure: The rotation-based commitment permits multiple distinct valid openings when the opening offset is chosen to compensate for the rotation.
tasks.expected_attack_outcome: produce two distinct opening pairs accepted for the same commitment
tasks.required_positive_control: Run ordinary commitment API behavior tests; they are compatibility checks, not proof of binding.

tasks.known_failure: Reusing a common XOR mask causes ciphertext pairs to reveal the XOR and Hamming-distance relationships of the plaintexts.
tasks.expected_attack_outcome: compute a plaintext relationship directly from two ciphertexts without the mask
tasks.required_positive_control: Run a non-security algebra round-trip and label it as algebra only.

tasks.security_notion: semantic equivalence of encrypted and plaintext aggregation
tasks.known_failure: For an even contributor count, a local tie resolves differently after masking can be removed, so encrypted aggregate output can disagree with the plaintext bundle.
tasks.expected_attack_outcome: produce the explicit even-count counterexample and explain the tie behavior
tasks.required_positive_control: Run the existing odd-count exactness test separately; do not generalize it to all counts.

tasks.security_notion: distinct context separation with independent secret entropy
tasks.known_failure: A linear pre-hash combination of sensor values admits distinct input tuples that cancel to the same encoded context; hashing afterward cannot restore distinctions lost before hashing.
tasks.expected_attack_outcome: construct two distinct sensor tuples with identical pre-hash context output
tasks.required_positive_control: Verify the candidate uses independent secret input and a standard KDF; do not treat a hash of public context as secret key material.

tasks.known_failure: A small deterministic sensor context domain can be enumerated; hashing the public/quantized context does not create independent secret entropy.
tasks.expected_attack_outcome: enumerate the narrowed sensor component or show deterministic recovery
tasks.required_positive_control: Verify the resulting value is treated as public context only, never as a secret key.
